title: Henrik goes to court over his rent
topic: A tenant and a landlord go to court over a contract: Henrik's contract fixes the rent, the landlord demands more, a lawyer takes the case, the judge hears both sides at a hearing and rules for Henrik

notes: Formulation A, domain law (domain control: State 2143 sits near the law domain in the atlas). Ten meaning units: Henrik rents a flat / the contract sets the rent for five years / the landlord demands more / Henrik refuses in a letter / a lawyer takes the case / the court schedules the hearing / the judge hears both sides / the landlord's lawyer cites a clause / Henrik shows the signed contract / the judge rules for Henrik. Subjects alternate between the protagonist (Henrik), other people (landlord, lawyer, judge, the landlord's lawyer), institutions (the court) and a document (the contract), so C3 switches cross real subject-verb agreement. No separable German verbs ('festlegen', 'ablehnen', 'ansetzen', 'anhören', 'vorlegen' avoided: 'regelt', 'verweigert', 'plant', 'hört', 'zeigt'); 'übernimmt' is inseparable. 'Henrik' is the only proper name (genitive 'Henriks' in unit 10). Present tense and positive polarity; unit 9 reads naturally in German, units 1 and 10 in English.
